subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Should maintainers sponsor a current-main repro/proof pass for this exec redirect corruption report before allowing a fix PR?
rationale: The issue is concrete and plausible, but source inspection only proves the normal exec path should preserve command text; it does not prove where the reported shipped-version mutation happens.

options.title: Reproduce before fix
options.body: Run a focused packaged/current-main exec scenario and only queue implementation after the mutation boundary is identified.

options.title: Keep parked for reporter proof
options.body: Leave the issue open but require new logs or a recording before spending maintainer time on a repro lane.

options.title: Close after non-repro proof
options.body: If maintainers can show current main and the latest package preserve `2>&1` without corruption, close with the exact proof.

recommendation.title: Reproduce before fix
recommendation.body: Run a focused packaged/current-main exec scenario and only queue implementation after the mutation boundary is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across exec host routing, approval trust, and redirect-adjacent allowlist behavior.
